note: KERNEL floor PRs — human-only, prepared for owner gate. Each fix in axon/*; write-gate allows (dev-mode on) but NOTHING merges without owner 'gate on'.

prs.title: ADVISORY (kernel floor): gate fail-opens in dry_run_lint & write_barrier — OWNER ESCALATION

bugs.summary: The dry-run merge gate misses mutating ops written inline after an arrow because _MUTATING_OP is anchored to line-start, so an unguarded mutator that writes via `→ WRITE(...)` passes.
bugs.failure_scenario: _MUTATING_OP = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:WRITE|APPEND|MKDIR|...)\(") is applied with .match(ln), which only matches when the op is the first token on the line. AXON-LANG programs routinely write mutating ops inline after a conditional arrow (e.g. code-dev-safety-audit-structure.md lines 86-87: `IF m ENDS-WITH "/" → MKDIR(...)` / `ELSE → WRITE(...)`). I created a mutator code-dev-merge.md with NO dry-run guard whose only mutations are `IF ready ≡ true → WRITE(...)` / `ELSE → MKDIR(...)`; run_check() returned ok=true, violations=[], hint 'all whatif-reachable mutators are dry-guarded' because first_mut resolved to None. A whatif dry-run of such a program would perform real destructive writes while the gate reports the promise is honored.

bugs.summary: _GUARD.search matches the dry-run token inside a `#` comment (no comment stripping), so a mutator whose real executable guard was removed but whose descriptive comment still mentions W:code-dev-dry-run passes the gate despite unguarded writes.
bugs.failure_scenario: check_program computes guard_at = first line where _GUARD (r"W:code-dev-dry-run") matches, without excluding comment lines. All four current mutators carry a leading comment like `# C8 dry-run guard — code-dev whatif arms W:code-dev-dry-run` (e.g. code-dev-divide.md line 52). I built code-dev-divide.md whose ONLY pre-op occurrence of the token is that comment (real `IF RETRIEVE(W:code-dev-dry-run)` guard deleted) followed by unguarded MKDIR(...)/WRITE(...); run_check() returned ok=true, violations=[]. Deleting the actual runtime guard is not caught as long as the human-readable comment remains, defeating whatif's 'no writes' contract.

bugs.summary: os.open() writes/truncations of protected subtrees bypass the write-barrier because os.open raises the 'open' audit event with mode=None, which _hook treats as a read and lets through.
bugs.failure_scenario: In an armed unattended child, `python3 -c "import os; fd=os.open('axon/KERNEL-SLIM.md', os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC); os.write(fd,b'')"` truncates the kernel floor. CPython raises audit event 'open' with args ('axon/KERNEL-SLIM.md', None, flags); _hook line 99-100 sets mode=args[1]=None, then `if mode is None: return` short-circuits before any _protected_hit check, so the mutation is ALLOWED. Demonstrated live: builtin open('a') is REFUSED but os.open with O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC on the same kernel file (and on a delete-protected workspace/programs file) is ALLOWED. This is the exact computed-path residual (os.open is listed in shell.py::_INTERP_WRITE_CALL) that shell.py delegates to G1c, so the backstop fails open on its own threat model. The write intent lives in the flags (args[2]) which the hook never inspects.

prs.title: ADVISORY (kernel floor): KERNEL-SLIM active-program interrupt gate integrity

bugs.summary: Interrupt-gate ABORT branch clears W:_interrupt-pending-input on line 258, then tries to EXEC that same (now-empty) key on line 260, so the user's new action is silently dropped on abort.
bugs.failure_scenario: A multi-step program is running (W:active-phase non-terminal). User types a new command 'deploy the app'; the gate stores it in W:_interrupt-pending-input (line 227) and prompts K/I/A. User chooses A (abort). Branch runs: line 257 sets active-phase to :aborted, line 258 CLEAR(W:_interrupt-pending-input) makes it ∅, then line 260 EXEC(W:_interrupt-pending-input) executes ∅ — a no-op. The program is aborted but 'deploy the app' is never run, contradicting the option label 'abort — discard program + run my new action'. (The I branch on line 253 does NOT clear first, so only ABORT loses the input.)

bugs.summary: Interrupt gate binds 'answer <- input' from the SAME input that triggered the interrupt, not from the K/I/A reply, so none of the K/I/A handler branches (lines 243/246/254) can execute on the prompt turn; and because the gate re-fires on EVERY input before parsing (line 208), the K/I/A reply on the next turn re-enters the ELSE branch and overwrites W:_interrupt-pending-input.
bugs.failure_scenario: Program running; user types 'show weather'. Gate stores 'show weather' (line 227), renders the K/I/A prompt, then line 242 sets answer <- input = 'show weather'. answer is not 'K'/'I'/'A'/'' so lines 243/246/254 all fail — nothing executes, the program stalls. Next turn user types 'I': gate fires again (line 208, 'fires on EVERY user input, BEFORE command parsing'), phase still active, 'i' is not in continuation-cmds (line 221) and not ^\d+$, so ELSE runs again — line 227 overwrites W:_interrupt-pending-input with 'I', destroying the original 'show weather', and re-renders the prompt. The interrupt/abort choices are unreachable and the original command is lost.

bugs.summary: `matches` operator with an invalid regex RHS raises re.error, which is neither ParseError nor EvalError and is never caught, crashing the CLI and any workflow-gate caller instead of returning the uniform error envelope.
bugs.failure_scenario: Predicate `name matches "["` with ctx `{"state":{"name":"abc"}}`: _cmp reaches re.search("[","abc") which raises re.error('unterminated character set'). main() only catches (ParseError, EvalError), so the process exits with a traceback (verified) and non-JSON output. As a library gate evaluator this propagates an uncaught exception up through goal-acceptance/synapse/workflow gates, breaking the documented 'error+message always present' contract that lets gate-walkers distinguish a broken predicate from a false one.

bugs.summary: `in` operator guards the RHS type but not LHS/RHS compatibility: `<non-string> in <string>` raises TypeError, which is not caught by main()'s (ParseError, EvalError) handler and crashes.
bugs.failure_scenario: Predicate `5 in name` with ctx `{"state":{"name":"abc"}}`: b="abc" passes the isinstance(b,(list,tuple,str)) guard, then `5 in "abc"` raises TypeError('in <string> requires string as left operand, not int') (verified). Uncaught, so the tool aborts with a traceback / the gate evaluation crashes instead of returning a clean type_mismatch error.

bugs.summary: Data source is selected with a truthiness test (`if args.data`) instead of a None check, so an empty `--data ''` falls through to `open(args.data_file)` with args.data_file=None, raising an uncaught TypeError.
bugs.failure_scenario: `python tools/validator.py --data '' --type object`: the mutually-exclusive group sets args.data='' and args.data_file=None. Line 40 evaluates `args.data` as falsy and runs `json.load(open(None))`, raising TypeError('expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not NoneType') (verified traceback). This is not in the caught (JSONDecodeError, FileNotFoundError) tuple, so the user gets a crash instead of the clean {"error": "Data error: ..."} envelope they'd get for other bad JSON.

bugs.summary: main() calls args.func(args) but never propagates the function's return value to sys.exit, so cmd_generate/cmd_query/cmd_validate's `return 1` error paths exit 0.
bugs.failure_scenario: Running `programs_registry.py --workspace <ws-with-no-programs-dir> generate` prints {"ok": false, "error": "no programs/ dir ..."} yet the process exits 0 (verified empirically); likewise `query`/`validate` against a not-yet-generated REGISTRY.json return 1 internally but exit 0. Consumers that read the exit code treat these failures as success: freshness.refresh() records report['rc']['program_registry']=0, and synapse_scaffold.register() returns 0. Contrast cmd_check, which correctly sys.exit(2). The masked-error paths are a silent fail-open on the registry writer/validator.

bugs.summary: Health score is read via kv-store with an L: key, which kv_store.py refuses and which no longer holds the value, so score is always None and self-care always reports health as unknown / needs-attention.
bugs.failure_scenario: health.py --persist has written L:health-score=95 to workspace/memory/longterm/health-score.md. `self-care check` calls _axon('kv-store','get','--key','L:health-score'); kv_store.py:46-51 rejects the L: namespace, printing {"error": ...} and exiting 2. _loads gives {'error':...}, hs.get('found') is falsy, so score=None. run_check sets health.ok via `score is None` -> True but appends 'health: unknown - run health-check' to needs_attention and reports overall status 'needs-attention', despite a healthy persisted score. The correct reader is memory.py --scope L --key health-score.

bugs.summary: complete-claim check uses a substring test `"complete" in (status+" "+phase)`, which matches the substring inside 'incomplete', producing a false complete-claim-unbacked finding.
bugs.failure_scenario: A dev-project _meta.md has `status: incomplete` and its manifest has a non-done phase (consistent with being incomplete). pointer_check evaluates `"complete" in ("incomplete" + " " + phase)` -> True, then lists the non-done phases and emits a 'complete-claim-unbacked' finding claiming the project 'claims complete but manifest has non-done phases', the exact opposite of reality, adding a spurious item to needs_attention.

prs.title: ADVISORY (kernel floor): kernel tool logic/format (lib ts, clock, liveness, redact, rules_loader)

bugs.summary: In-process usage_record writes ts as isoformat()+"Z" ("...+00:00Z"), which usage.py's readers cannot parse with datetime.fromisoformat, so those entries are silently dropped from all windowed queries.
bugs.failure_scenario: The orchestrator/hooks record a program run via _axon_lib.usage_record(ws, kind='program', name='menu'). Line 173 appends a JSONL entry to workspace/memory/longterm/usage-log.jsonl with ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() + "Z", e.g. '2026-07-27T09:28:38.395+00:00Z'. That string has both a +00:00 offset AND a trailing Z, which is invalid ISO-8601; datetime.fromisoformat() raises ValueError on it (verified on the repo's Python 3.10.12). usage.py's read_entries (line 67, used by `usage top` and `usage suggest`), aggregate (line 136, `--since`), and cmd_prune (line 248) all parse ts via datetime.fromisoformat inside a try/except that skips the entry on failure. Result: (a) `usage top --window 7d` and `usage suggest --window 30d` (the defaults) drop every in-process-recorded run, so frequently-run programs never surface as compile candidates; (b) `usage prune --before 90d` treats them as unparseable and keeps them forever (unbounded log growth). usage.py's own CLI `record` uses now_iso() WITHOUT the trailing 'Z' (line 33), so the two writers to the same log file disagree on ts format and only the CLI-written entries are readable.

bugs.summary: clock's `unix` field is computed with naive-UTC `.timestamp()`, which Python interprets as LOCAL time, so `unix` is wrong (off by the host's UTC offset) on any non-UTC machine while iso/date/time stay correct.
bugs.failure_scenario: `_now()` returns a naive datetime from `datetime.datetime.utcnow()` (or `utcfromtimestamp`). In `_fmt`, `int(now.timestamp())` treats that UTC wall-clock as local time. On the user's Europe/Amsterdam host (UTC+2 in July), running `clock` emits `unix` = true_unix - 7200 (verified: -7200s), i.e. 2 hours behind, while the `iso`/`date`/`time` fields report the correct UTC instant. Any program that consumes `unix` for age/ordering/arithmetic (or compares it against `iso`) gets a value hours off from reality on every non-UTC runner.

bugs.summary: The sentinel-seam caller pattern r'\bauthorized\s*\(' for autonomous_mode.authorized matches unrelated English prose, so a genuinely-dead governance seam is reported as wired.
bugs.failure_scenario: check_sentinel_seams() scans the production corpus for callers of the S1 seam autonomous_mode.authorized using patterns including r'\bauthorized\s*\('. workspace/programs/quality-loop.md contains the prose 'S-fixes authorized (earned, revocable)'; \s* matches the space so 'authorized (' matches. Verified live: that prose line counts as a 'caller'. Therefore, even if autonomous_mode.authorized() has ZERO real production call sites (the audit's #1 'coded, never called' defect), no dead-sentinel finding is emitted and run() reports ok, silently regressing the seam the lint exists to protect.

bugs.summary: Reported hit start/end offsets are relative to the progressively-redacted string, not the original text, so hits from any pattern after the first are misreported when an earlier pattern replaced text of a different length (contradicts the line-27 'original positions' contract).
bugs.failure_scenario: Input text `sk-` followed by 30 chars (33-char anthropic key) then ` AKIA1234567890123456`. The first pattern (anthropic-openai) replaces the 33-char key with the 27-char `[REDACTED:anthropic-openai]`, shrinking `out` by 6. The AWS pattern then runs on this shortened string and reports the AKIA hit's start/end 6 positions lower than its true offset in the original text, so any consumer using start/end to locate/highlight the secret in the original input indexes the wrong span.

bugs.summary: Dead-rule detection uses substring containment (`r["id"] not in log_text`), so a rule id that is a prefix of another (R-1 vs R-10) is falsely counted as referenced and never flagged dead.
bugs.failure_scenario: audit() marks a rule dead only if `r["id"] not in log_text`. Rule ids are `R-\d+`, so 'R-1' is a substring of 'R-10', 'R-11', etc. With rules R-1 and R-10 in safety/rules.md and a workspace/log/_actions.log that references only 'R-10', I called audit(): dead=[] (checked=2). R-1, which is genuinely never referenced, is reported as alive because 'R-1' in 'R-10' is True. The catalog-hygiene audit therefore silently omits any low-numbered rule whose number is a prefix of a referenced higher-numbered rule.

prs.title: ADVISORY (kernel floor): compiler template defects (chat-session, feedback-loop, qc-workflow)

bugs.summary: Save Output invokes the translate program with the arg key `input:` instead of the required `source:`, so translate receives no content and hard-fails.
bugs.failure_scenario: Instantiate chat-session with output-path="workspace/out.md" (any output-format). After Execute Goal populates W:chat-output, Save Output runs EXEC(translate, {input: W:chat-output, format: "doc"}). The semantic translate program (workspace/programs/translate.md) requires the `source` input; its Step 1 sees source=∅ -> W:content=∅ -> FAIL(T-current, "No content to translate"). W:formatted-output is never produced, WRITE writes nothing/garbage, yet Close still logs and records the chat output as saved. (Secondary: the template's output-format enum {doc|report|list|raw} also offers `list`/`raw`, which are not valid translate formats [explanation|report|doc|audit].)

bugs.summary: Actor-failure branch falls through to EVAL instead of skipping the iteration; its eval-result write is dead and EVAL runs on empty/FAIL input.
bugs.failure_scenario: When the actor EXEC returns ∅ or FAIL (line 71), the branch sets eval-result←{score:0,...} (line 74) and the comment on line 75 claims 'Skip to next iteration'. But there is no CONTINUE/loop-restart and Phase 3 (line 79) is unconditional, so control falls straight into EVAL(W:actor-output=∅, criteria, tolerance)→eval-result. The score:0 write is immediately overwritten (dead write), and EVAL is invoked on the exact empty/failed output the branch was meant to avoid — producing a garbage score (or crash) that then drives the passed/UNTIL decision instead of a clean retry.

bugs.summary: Slack alert message interpolates {W:batch-key}, a memory key that is never stored.
bugs.failure_scenario: On escalation, TOOL(notify, ...) builds message "QC ALERT: {W:fail-count} failures on {{item-name}} batch {W:batch-key}". The batch list was stored to W:batch (line 24); no key named W:batch-key exists. So {W:batch-key} resolves to ∅/blank and the alert reads 'batch ' with no identifier. The correct token is the template param {{batch-key}} (used correctly on line 52 EMIT and line 61 APPEND), or {W:batch}.

bugs.summary: RAND(W:batch, W:sample-size) misuses RAND — there is no 'sample N without replacement' form.
bugs.failure_scenario: The line claims 'random sample without replacement' and stores the result as W:sample, then the loop does `LOOP(∀ item ∈ W:sample)`. But RAND (LANG.md EXT-002) is only `RAND(list)` -> one element, or `RAND(min,max)` -> one integer. With two args the second being a count, it is parsed as RAND(min=W:batch, max=W:sample-size), yielding a single scalar, not a size-N subset. The inspection loop then iterates over a non-list (or a single item), so the QC never samples the intended sample-size items.

prs.title: ADVISORY (kernel floor): kernel program specs (dev-new, plan-list, register-preference)

bugs.summary: Scaffold template hardcodes DONE(dev-new) instead of DONE({W:dev-new-name}), so every new program created by dev-new terminates with the wrong program name.
bugs.failure_scenario: User runs `dev-new my-tool "desc"`. dev-new WRITEs the scaffold (lines 28-49) in which the header, GUARD FAIL, and banner all interpolate {W:dev-new-name} to 'my-tool', but line 48 emits the literal DONE(dev-new). The generated workspace/programs/my-tool.md therefore ends with `DONE(dev-new)`. When the user later runs `my-tool`, it emits DONE(dev-new) — closing/marking-done the wrong program/process, and my-tool never gets a matching DONE, violating PROGRAMS.md's 'DONE([name]) matching the filename' contract.

bugs.summary: FIND used where a filter is needed — only the first active/completed plan is ever captured, so the list under-reports.
bugs.failure_scenario: With 4 active plans in workspace/plans/, `active ← FIND(plans, status="active")` returns only the FIRST matching plan object (FIND per LANG.md EXT-003 = 'first item where cond is true, or ∅'), not a list. Downstream `→ "ACTIVE ({COUNT(active)})"` prints '(1)' and `∀ p in SORT(active, ...)` iterates a single object, so 3 of the 4 active plans are silently omitted from the menu. Same defect for `complete ← FIND(plans, status="completed")` on line 23. The code needs a filter/WHERE (as mode-run.md uses `progs WHERE ...`), not FIND.

bugs.summary: OUTPUT section interpolates W:pref-topic/pref-key/pref-value after they were CLEARed three lines earlier, so the user-facing confirmation renders with blank fields.
bugs.failure_scenario: User runs `register-preference output output-mode PYTHON_FAST`. The WRITE section correctly persists the value to disk and to W:user-prefs, then executes CLEAR(W:pref-topic), CLEAR(W:pref-key), CLEAR(W:pref-value) at lines 42-44. Execution then reaches the OUTPUT section (lines 46-53), which interpolates the now-empty keys. The user sees '▶ register-preference  ·  ' (empty topic), 'Saved:  = ' (empty key and value), and 'File: workspace/preferences/.md' (empty topic) instead of the actual saved preference — a broken/misleading confirmation. Fix: move the three CLEAR ops to after the OUTPUT section (or before DONE).
